Humayun Bashar, Advocate -----For the Petitioner. 
No one appears -----For the Respondents.
parties:
Saiful Islam (Md) ----- Petitioner
Vs.
Secretary Ministry of Housing and Public Works, and others-----Respondents
full_judgment:
AKM Shahidul Huq J: On an application under Article 102 of the Constitution of the Peoples Republic of Bangladesh at the instance of the petitioner a Rule Nisi has been issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the discriminatory treatment to the petitioner and inaction of the respondents in giving allotment of a plot in the extended Uttara Third Residential Area (third phase) Project as affected person in compliance with the provision of Article 8 (kba) প্লট বরাদ্দ নীতিমালা Rajdhani Unnayan Kartripakba as well as of the decision taken in the Board meeting of Rajdhani Unnayan Kartripakba dated 23-9-2010 and 26-9-2010 (Annexure-E) should not be declared to have been done without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and why a direction should not be given upon the respondents to give allotment of a plot to the petitioner in the extended Uttara Residential Area (third phase) Project as affected person vide Award Serial Nos. 368/1, 369/3 and 370/2 and security deposit slip No. 10023 and or pass such other or further order or orders passed as to this court may seem fit and proper.

2. Relevant facts necessary for disposal of the instant rule is that the petitioner acquired 17 decimals of land at District Dhaka, formerly Police Station Mirpur, Mouza Bounia, SA Plot No. 245/246/248 and RS Plot Nos. 366/370/371 from its lawful owner Serajul Haque Prodhan and MrsRokeya Begum, by virtue of a deed of Hebabil-ewaj vide No. 2145 dated 5-6-2000.

3. The petitioner got possession of the said land and got his name mutated under mutation case No. 12421 of 2002, 12412 of 2002 and 12423 of 2002 and paid rents to the Government in respect of his total land measuring 17 decimals.

4. While the petitioner was owning and possessing the said land, the Government decided to acquire the same along with some other lands for the requiring body namely Rajdhani Unnayan Kartripakha and ultimately the land was acquired under LA Case No.6 of 2001-2002 and duly served notice upon the petitioner.

5. The petitioner applied for compensation award against his acquired land by submitting all relevant title deeds and papers and the office of the Additional Deputy Commissioner (LA) having been satisfied as to the ownership of the petitioner gave compensation money with award.

6. The requiring body namely Rajdhahi Unnayan Kartripakba published and advertisement inviting applications from the interested person for allotment of plots under the project namely, "Extended Uttara Third Residential Area (third phase) project hereinafter referred to. as the "Project" and the petitioner being affected person in response to the said advertisement, filed application for getting a plot measuring 3 katha by depositing required amount of Taka 75,000.

7. The persons whose land is acquired is entitled to get priority of allotment Of the plot if the acquisition is for the residential purpose and in this regard a gazette was published on 15th January 1970 as Dhaka gazette wherein it was provided that "Subject to the provision of clause B of sub-section of section 101 of the Act valid application of the person who had either land or residential house in the area acquired for the development of Township, has have the first preference for allotment provided be applied and fulfill other condition RAJUK set up a nitimala for allotment of plot of the affected person as 8 (ka) and 8(kha) and the petitioner is within the Nitimala of 8(kba). The petitioner's land is acquired and he has fulfilled all the required conditions and made application in proper form.

8. The Rajdhani Unnayan Kartripakha already started giving allotment and also allotted many plots to their chosen persons and though already more than 8 years elapsed from the date of filing application with requisite amount of Taka 75,000, the petitioner did not receive any response or information from the authority as to his allotment of the plot as he is entitled to get preference .in allotment of plot under the project.

9. The petitioner acquired the land measuring 17 decimals for residential purpose and except the said acquired land he has no other piece of land within Dhaka City Corporation and due to such acquisition, he become landless in the city.

10. It is evident from the minutes of the Board Meeting of Rajdhani Unnayan Kartripakha dated 23-9-2010 and 26-9-2010 that there is clear admission by RAJUK that the people whose 0.1650 acre of land or more than that have been acquired are entitled to have a plot and accordingly, the said Board meeting recommended allotment of plots in favour of 568 affected persons.

11. RAJUK gave allotment of plot to the 568 affected persons as per Nitimala enunciated in 8 (ka) and 8 (kha) and the matter was published in Daily News Paper namely Daily "Samakal" on 24-10-2010.

12. The provision regarding allotment of the plots is that the affected persons shall have first preference for getting allotment, but the respondents without considering the legitimate right of the petitioner already allotted many plots to their chosen person and not taking any steps for giving allotment in favour of the petitioner and, as such, the discriminatory treatment and inaction of the respondents in giving allotment of a plot in the project is liable to be declared to have been done without lawful authority and be of no legal effect.

13. Mr Md Humayun Bashar, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner and no one appears on behalf of the respondent No. 2 to oppose the rule.

14. Mr Md Humayun Bashar, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that the provisions regarding allotment of the plots is that the affected persons shall have first preference for getting allotment, but the respondents without considering the legitimate right of the petitioner already allotted many plots to their chosen persons and not taking any steps for giving allotment in favour of the petitioner and, as such, the discriminatory treatment and -inaction .of the respondents in giving allotment of a plot .in the project is liable to be declared to have been done without lawful authority and be of no legal effect.

15. He next submits that since 568 affected persons have been selected for allotment, on the criterion that they are awardees of 0.1650 acre of land, the petitioner being equally' affected standing on the same footing is entitled to have a plot but the respondents with malafide motive discriminating the petitioner with them depriving his legitimate right and, as such, the discriminatory treatment inaction of the respondents in giving allotment of a plot to the petitioner in the project is liable to be declared to have been done without lawful authority and be of no legal effect and the respondents are liable to be directed to give allotment of a plot to the petitioner from the project.

16. Learned Advocate further submits that since the petitioner is an awardee of 0.17 acres of land, he is entitled to have a plot under Article 8 of the প্লট বরাদ্দ নীতিমালা RAJUK as well as the  decision and recommendation taken in the Board Meeting of RAJUK dated 23-9-2010 and 26-9- 2010 and more so, 568 affected persons, having selected for allotment on criterion as above and, as such, the discriminatory treatment and in action of the respondents in giving allotment of a plot in the project is liable to be declared to have been done without lawful authority and be of no legal effect and the respondents are liable to be directed to give allotment of a plot to the petitioner from, the project.

17. He lastly submits that the inaction of the respondents to comply with the Article 8 (kha) of the প্লট বরাদ্দ নীতিমালা of RAJUK as well as its decision equally in respect of the petitioner like as the 568 others who have been selected for allotment of plot is discriminatory, arbitrary, malafide and a clear violation of the fundamental rights of the petitioner guaranteed under Article 27 and 31 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh.

18. Learned Advocate in support of his contention refers an unreported decision of this Hon'ble Division passed in writ petition No. 1781 of 2011.

19. No one appears to oppose the rule on behalf of the respondent.

20. Heard the learned Advocate perused the writ petition filed under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh and the annexure filed thereto and considered the material on record.

21. It appears from annexure H, minutes of the 9th Board meeting of RAJUK dated 23-9- 2010 and 26-9-2010, that the concerned Ministry had recommended for allotment of plots in favour of the awardees of 0.1650 acres of land as affected persons. The Board of RAJUK also decided to allot plots to 560 persons on the criterion that 0.1650 acres of land had been acquired from each of them and, as such, they were entitled to a plot under Article 8 (kha) of the প্লট বরাদ্দ নীতিমালা of RAJUK. However, it appears from the same minutes that, the fate of 54 persons including the petitioners, whose awards had been subsequently added on their applications to make them eligible for allotment on the same criterion, remained pending.

<u>22. Since 560 persons have been selected for allotment of plots on consideration that they are awardees of 0.1650 acres of land, we do not see any valid reason for excluding the petitioner from such benefit. Since they are equally affected, although by subsequent addition of their awards, We do not find any legal reason for denial of their such entitlements when people standing on the same footing were selected for such allotment. Since main criterion as set by RAJUK is awardee of 0.1650 acres of land and names of 560 selected persons have been published in the daily newspaper on such consideration, we are of the view that the petitioner are also jointly entitled to have a 5 (five) katha plot allotted in their favour if lands are available with RAJUK for such allotment.</u>

23. We find support of this view in a decision of our Apex Court held in RAJUK vs Jahanara Begum, reported in 12 BLT (AD) (2004) page 222 = 57 DLR (AD) 80 wherein modifying the order passed by the High Court Division, the Appellate Division directed the RAJUK to scrutiny the petition filed by the writ petitioners for allotment of plot and to allot plots in their favour if they satisfied the condition and criteria set down by the RAJUK entitling a person to have allotment of plot as affected person provided RAJUK has available lands for such allotment.

24. In view of the said decision of our Apex Court, we hold that since the petitioners has prima-facie fulfilled the criterion in the instant case, namely he is awardee of 0.1650 acres of land like other 560 selected allottees, he is also entitled to have a 5 (five) katha plot allotted jointly in his favour as applied for provided RAJUK has available land for such allotment.

Accordingly, RAJUK is directed to scrutinize petitioners' application receiving code No. 15227 for allotment of plot in the extended Uttara 3rd residential project and allot a 5 (five) katha plot in his favour provided RAJUK has available lands for such allotment. The above process should be completed within 2 (two) months from the date of receipt of the copy of this judgment and order, with the above directions and observations, the rule is disposed of, without any order as to cost. Transmit a copy of this judgment to the concern authority forthwith for information and necessary action.

End.
